data.title: “Why are we excluded?” CUPE personal support workers to rally to be treated like every other profession in Ontario
data.description: In Toronto, there is growing concern among Personal Support Workers (PSWs) about their treatment within the healthcare system. The newly established regulatory body for PSWs by the Ford administration, the Health and Supportive Care Providers Oversight Authority (HSCPOA), is facing criticism for not including any PSWs on its board of directors. Tera Engley, President of CUPE Local132 and a PSW, highlighted the issue, stating that PSWs have often been marginalized by both management and the government. The absence of PSWs on the HSCPOA board is seen as a reinforcement of this marginalization. This has sparked debates about the representation and recognition of PSWs in the healthcare sector.

data.title: Ingalls Shipbuilding’s Virtual Reality Welding Lab Surpasses 1,000 Trainees
data.description: PASCAGOULA, Mississippi - In September 18, 2026, it was announced that Ingalls Shipbuilding division's Virtual Reality (VR) Welding Lab, owned by HII (NYSE: HII), has successfully trained over 1,000 individuals since its launch in January 2025. This achievement underscores the significance of Ingalls' dedication to cutting-edge training tools and the joint efforts of the U.S. Navy, AccelerateMS, and Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College (MGCCC) in establishing the lab.

data.title: PAL Airlines Flight Attendants File for Conciliation
data.description: In St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, flight attendants at PAL Airlines are seeking conciliation with the federal labour board as negotiations have failed to make significant advancement on important matters. Represented by CUPE 5451, the flight attendants have been in talks with PAL Airlines since the spring of 2025, following the expiration of their previous collective agreement on April 30, 2025. This move comes as a response to unresolved issues despite their crucial role in ensuring passenger safety and maintaining community connections within PAL's network.
